From the judge's explanation

To the rider and the driver: this dispute is decided on the trip's own evidence, and the outcome is that the $4.50 no-show cancellation fee stands as charged and the driver is paid the platform's 80% share, $3.60.

How to appeal: Either party may appeal once within 30 days. A different human reviewer hears it, and only record evidence may be added.

POL-GEN-05: the monetary effect is SGD 3.60 against an execution threshold of SGD 8.00. It does not exceed the threshold, so the amount is executed automatically on issue, subject to POL-GEN-04.

Read POL-GEN-04 in full
Every ruling issued without human review is a provisional ruling. Either party may appeal it once, within 30 days of the trip or of the ruling's issue, whichever is later, by lodging the appeal with the platform's help channel. An appeal (a) is heard by a human reviewer who did not take part in any earlier review of the same trip; (b) may add only record-type evidence - a GPS export, a fare or payment statement, an ERP gantry record with gantry name, entry time and cashcard statement, a call log, a photograph with its capture time - and may not add or amend a party statement; (c) suspends execution of any amount not yet executed and freezes it until decided, and where the amount was executed under POL-GEN-05 before the appeal, a successful appeal reverses it; (d) may not be withdrawn and re-lodged. A second appeal on the same trip, an appeal lodged after 30 days, or an appeal that adds only statements is refused. The appeal decision is recorded as a human closure under POL-GEN-06, enters the precedent store, and is final on the platform. This clause licenses no ruling value: an appeal is a route to human review, not a ruling, and it is lodged after a ruling has issued.

Each draft's own explanation

To the rider and the driver: this dispute is decided on the trip's own evidence, and the outcome is that the $4.50 no-show cancellation fee stands as charged and the driver is paid the platform's 80% share, $3.60. Why the fee stands. A no-show fee is chargeable only if all four parts of POL-NS-01 hold. They do. (a) The trip record (EV-TRIP-02752, weight 1.0) carries the driver's 'arrived' event at 22:06:11. (b) The GPS trace (EV-GPS-02752, weight 1.0) places the driver inside the 50 m STANDARD arrival radius at and after that moment: 44 accuracy-qualifying fixes in one unbroken in-geofence run opening at 22:06:11, with a closest approach of 0.0 m and POL-NS-02's three-consecutive-fix test met. The STANDARD zone class is read from the trip record, not assumed. (c) That single run lasts 434 seconds (22:06:11 to 22:13:25), comfortably above the 180-second free waiting period in force for this trip (trip_record.platform_policy.free_wait_sec = 180; no_show_threshold_sec is null, so no longer threshold applies) — a surplus of 254 seconds. The dwell is measured from the first qualifying in-geofence fix, not the tap, and the two are the same second (dwell_start_offset_sec 0.0). (d) There is no boarding (started_at and ended_at are null) and the driver terminated at 22:13:25 under RIDER_NO_SHOW, well after the required dwell elapsed at 22:09:11. POL-NS-05 is not engaged: the arrival tap coincides with the first in-geofence fix, so the trace does not put the driver more than 300 m from the pin or moving at 15 km/h at the marker; there is no false arrival and no false-arrival referral. The rider's routes were each tested and each fails. POL-NS-06 has no shortfall to refund — the dwell exceeds the minimum by 254 seconds (the cited advisory limb is irrelevant, and in any case no advisory covers this pickup). POL-NS-02 / POL-NS-12: the arrival marker is a driver BUTTON press, not GPS_AUTO, so the platform's timing events do not substitute for the export — but the export itself carries the arrival and the dwell, so the limb is met on the trace.
